chairs_names: Jennifer Trizuto, DPT (Speaker) | Becki Cleveland, PhD (Speaker)
chairs_geography: Sutter Tracy Community Hospital, San Mateo, California | University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Chapel Hill, North Carolina
description:
Learning Objectives::
Describe how industrial food systems, agricultural practices, and climate change are degrading the shared environmental inputs-food, water, and air-that directly affect human healthExplain how nutritional depletion from soil degradation, subsidy-driven food diversion, and environmental toxin exposure create a compromised food chain that reaches the rheumatic patient's plateIdentify the mechanisms by which dietary patterns drive systemic inflammation and disease activity in common rheumatic conditions, including RA, SLE, gout, and osteoarthritis, with the gut microbiome as the central mechanistic hubSummarize the evidence for whole-food, plant-based, and Mediterranean dietary patterns as therapeutic interventions in rheumatic disease-and their dual benefit for planetary healthExplain the emerging evidence for fiber-rich diets as a tool for mitigating environmental toxin burden, and communicate this evidence appropriately to patients seeking integrative approachesApply practical dietary counseling strategies and articulate the rheumatology professional's advocacy roleâat the level of the patient encounter, the clinical institution, and health policy
